title: The checkmark example animates like somebody who knows what they are doing
goal: The checkmark switching on is the example that has to sell the whole feature, and right now it does three things at once, too quickly, with everything starting at the same moment. It should read as one deliberate idea: the circle draws, then the check draws, and the fill arrives by being revealed upward rather than by a pile of separate changes all firing together.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-15 after reading the redone mocks: "the chekmark on shoudl reveal the fill upwards, it's doing too many things. the checkmark on is animating too fast and shows no initial delay to draw the circle and then the check."

The checkmark appears in docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-drawon-wt.html and again in time-compare.html. Whichever page carries it, both must end up telling the same story, so fix it once and make the other follow rather than leaving two versions of the same example.

What is worth taking from this beyond the one example: the mock is demonstrating the feature by animating everything at once, which is exactly what a person who has never animated anything would do, and exactly what the app should be teaching them not to do. The example is the argument for delays and sequencing existing at all, so it has to USE them visibly. If the timing surface in the page cannot show a delay before a part starts, that is a finding about the surface and not just about the example.

TWO THINGS THE USER LIKED AND THAT MUST SURVIVE THIS EDIT, said in the same message: "i like the timing dock, and i like the custom easing adjuster." Do not redesign either while fixing the example. If the fix needs something from them, extend rather than replace, and say so in the audit.
acceptance: The fill arrives by being revealed upward, as one move, rather than by several properties changing at the same time
The circle and the check are sequenced, not simultaneous: the circle completes, then the check begins, with a stated pause between them
The whole thing is slow enough to read: the duration is chosen deliberately and the number is written in the page, not left at whatever it was
Every part of the sequence has an explicit start time, so the page shows that delays are a first class thing you set rather than something the app decides
The page shows the timing laid out, so a person can see the circle, the pause and the check as three things on a strip rather than reading it in prose
The example uses the per-property model the rest of the pages use, and no part of it is a named preset
It still holds together at the size an icon is really used, not only blown up on the page
Audit under queue/audits/ with the sequence captured frame by frame, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. Reproduced the complaint by reading the page's own numbers rather than trusting the prose. Three real faults, and they explain every word of the report.

(1) THE ARTWORK CONTRADICTS THE PANEL. The badge's CSS runs 'animation: ... infinite' on both strokes, while the Properties panel insists Repeat is Once and the step copy says 'a badge that draws itself over and over is a badge nobody trusts'. So the thing on screen is exactly what the page argues against: it redraws forever with no rest between laps, which reads as a flicker rather than a gesture. That alone is most of 'animating too fast'.

(2) THERE IS NO PAUSE, THERE IS AN OVERLAP, AND IT IS THE PAGE'S CENTREPIECE. Ring 0.50s at 0.00, check 0.35s at 0.42: the check starts 80ms BEFORE the ring closes, and step 6 spends its whole caption celebrating that as 'the entire craft of this scenario'. The user asked for the opposite, an initial delay so the circle draws and THEN the check does. The negative overlap is the thing being complained about, so it goes, and a stated hold replaces it.

(3) THERE IS NO FILL AT ALL. Nothing in the page can be revealed upward because the badge is two strokes on an empty artboard. So the report is not 'change how the fill animates', it is 'the example needs a fill, and it should arrive as one move'.

WHAT THE MOCK GETS WRONG BEYOND THE ONE EXAMPLE, which the task asked me to look for. The page cannot show a delay as anything a person can see: timing lives in an Order list of two rows in the side column, and a gap between two motions is a subtraction you do in your head. That is a finding about the SURFACE, not the example, and it is already the pending task rebuild-the-spinner-toggle-and-draw-on-flows-on. So this fix does the draw-on third of that task rather than inventing a second answer: Motion becomes a dock group beside Effects, and the timing dock goes across the bottom, exactly as the bell pages do it. That is also the two things the user said they liked, so it is extending them rather than redesigning them.

WHAT I AM CUTTING. The 'send it the other way round' step is a real idea but it is a fourth thing in a flow that is already being told it does too many things; the From row and the direction marker stay, the dedicated step goes, and the flow ends up the same length rather than longer.

WHAT 'REVEAL THE FILL UPWARDS' IS, in the per-property model and not as a preset called Reveal: the fill is a rectangle clipped to the ring, and what animates is its POSITION, 19 units below to 0. One property, one move, already the first item in the property menu. No new vocabulary, and the note can say plainly that it is not a fade and not a scale.

SECOND REVIEW, on the built page, in Chrome at 1500x1500 in both themes, stepping all eight steps. What I found and fixed while reviewing:

- The timing dock and the property menu overlapped: every popover was hand placed for the old 846px window and ran into the strip the step was asking you to read. Moved propMenu, curveMenu, repMenu and the curve editor; the curve editor now sits BESIDE the badge rather than on top of it, so you can watch what the curve does while you drag it.
- The 'done, then it rests' mark sat at 1200 on every step, including the ones where only 420 ms of motion existed. It now moves with what has been built: .2625, .2625, .5375, .75.
- The timing dock's length chip read '1.20 s' on step 1, before anything moved. Now 'nothing yet'.
- The four real-size previews kept showing the fill on the steps where the artboard hid it, and ran the check at its final timing during step 4 where the artboard ran it at zero. Both are now driven off the same classes as the artboard, so the small copies and the big one always agree. Verified by sampling getComputedStyle on both at 260 ms intervals: identical transforms through a whole cycle.
- The custom curve editor drew a curve that was not the four numbers under it. cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1) puts its handles at (20,30) and (30,0), not (20,44) and (70,0). On a page whose whole argument is that nobody can tell curves apart by reading their names, the drawing has to be the truth.
- The bars' aria-labels carried numbers that steps rewrite visibly but cannot rewrite in an attribute, so they went stale. They now name the bar instead.
- Properties showed 'Length —' for the Fill layer, which is a rectangle and has no path length. It gets its own Shape section (Size 18 x 18, Clipped to Ring).

WHAT I LEFT ROUGH, all of it in the audit's rough list too:
- left rough: the Motion group only ever shows one row, because it is the selected layer's motions exactly as Effects is. Correct model, possibly surprising. Not filed: it is the whole point of the dock existing, and the strip answers it.
- left rough: the preview loops while Repeat reads Once. The page says the replay is the preview and not the motion, in the Repeat menu note and in step 3. Not filed.
- left rough: the popovers are still taller than the space under their triggers, so they open a long way above them. A real menu flips the same way. Not filed.

ON THE TASK NOTE'S SECOND PAGE: the note says the checkmark 'appears again in time-compare.html'. It does not. time-compare only LINKS to this page and cites its Order list in one sentence; there is no second copy of the artwork to keep in step. That sentence and the matching paragraph in docs/design/animation-vs-video.md both now describe the strip, so nothing in the study still tells the old story.

BOTH THINGS THE USER SAID THEY LIKED SURVIVED AND WERE EXTENDED, NOT REDESIGNED. The timing dock is the same component as the bell pages' (same .track/.ruler/.bl-style bars, same collapse behaviour); what is new in it is the hold marker, which is a labelled box in the gap between two bars and nothing else. The custom easing adjuster is the same popover with the same readout; the only change is that its drawing now matches its numbers.

Rebuilt docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-drawon-wt.html so the success badge reads as one deliberate idea: ring draws 0-420 ms, a 180 ms HOLD drawn as a labelled gap on the strip, check 600-860, fill revealed upward 860-1200 by ONE property moving (a rectangle clipped to the ring, Position 0,18 to 0,0). 1.20 s end to end, stated in the page. Every part has an explicit Start, set in a field and drawn as a bar; step 4 builds the wrong version on purpose (both at 0, two bars with the same left edge) so the fix is visible rather than asserted. The Order list and the negative Overlap field are gone, replaced by the Motion dock group and the timing dock the bell pages use, which are the two surfaces the user said they liked, extended rather than redesigned. Also fixed a duplicate close button in the timing dock bar on all three animation pages (each hand-authored a .tl-close that dock.js also injects; verified two rendered buttons in Chrome before the fix). time-compare.html and docs/design/animation-vs-video.md updated so nothing still cites the Order list. Verified in Chrome across all eight steps in both themes: bars, hold, end mark, totals and chips agree at every step, the fill animates in the artboard and all four real-size previews in lockstep, no console errors; all seven mock gates pass. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-15-icon-drawon-sequencing.json with three captures. Commit 5aecb56e, pushed.
